axes.positive_pole: Introspective first-person Substack-style essays on self-acceptance, romance, ambition, and twentysomething life lessons.
axes.negative_pole: Corporate/technical pages about AI infrastructure, LLMs, agent frameworks, and ML research products.

axes.name: ai_alignment_discourse_vs_web_design_craft
axes.positive_pole: Long-form analytical writing about AI alignment, safety, misalignment risks, and the future of advanced AI systems, typically on rationalist/AI-research blogs.
axes.negative_pole: Personal portfolios, web-design inspiration galleries, and creative-coding/indie-web showcases focused on visual craft and aesthetics rather than written argument.

axes.name: startup_venture_capital_ness
axes.positive_pole: Pages about founding startups, venture capital, accelerators, and Silicon Valley career paths for aspiring entrepreneurs.
axes.negative_pole: Pages featuring literary poetry or technical machine-learning/interpretability content (neural network internals, transformers, attention).

axes.name: cultural_critique_vs_self_improvement
axes.positive_pole: Long-form cultural, philosophical, geopolitical, or literary commentary on civilization, ideology, and the human condition (often citing theorists, novels, or historical events).
axes.negative_pole: Practical first-person advice posts on personal productivity, learning, research methodology, and how to do great work as an individual.

axes.name: quantitative_business_analysis_vs_ai_creativity_reflection
axes.positive_pole: Pages presenting quantitative, formula-driven analyses of business, finance, startups, or computer-science algorithms with concrete metrics, math, and how-to mechanics.
axes.negative_pole: Personal landing pages and reflective essays by AI/HCI researchers and artists musing on creativity, human-AI interaction, and the philosophy of AI tools.

axes.name: intellectual_self_improvement_vs_relational_emotional
axes.positive_pole: Long-form essays and book recommendations on how to think, learn, do research, and solve hard problems—aimed at cultivating the reader's intellectual craft.
axes.negative_pole: Personal/cultural writing about relationships, dating, loneliness, and AI companions, or product pages about AI tools—focused on emotional life and contemporary tech culture rather than intellectual self-cultivation.

axes.name: personal_bio_vs_tech_essay
axes.positive_pole: Personal homepage/about-me pages or biographical profiles of individuals (typically young AI/tech researchers and founders) listing their education, jobs, and interests.
axes.negative_pole: Topical long-form essays and opinion pieces about software, web design, interfaces, or internet culture, written as arguments rather than self-introductions.

axes.name: relationships_and_social_connection_focus
axes.positive_pole: The page is an essay or guide centered on interpersonal connection—how to meet, befriend, converse with, or build community/trust with other people.
axes.negative_pole: The page is a personal essay about work, productivity, time, or life trajectory, with the individual's relationship to their own work/time as the central topic rather than relationships with others.

axes.name: commentary_vs_frontier_tech
axes.positive_pole: Personal blog-style commentary, criticism, and meta-discussion about the internet, AI discourse, and online culture (often opinionated essays reacting to other writing).
axes.negative_pole: Institutional or company-style announcements describing ambitious frontier science/engineering projects (biotech, energy, hardware, neuroscience, moonshots) and their technical missions.

axes.name: design_taste_and_craft_discourse
axes.positive_pole: Essays and studio/product pages centered on aesthetic taste, craft, and the artistry of design (visual, product, or brand-making) as the core subject.
axes.negative_pole: Utilitarian posts about personal-productivity systems, note-taking, second-brain tools, knowledge management, and lists of tools/tips for organizing information.
